mbm-2451.clue: My entrance begins with a teaspoon.
mbm-2451.quote: Backstage at our theater the cue bell broke. I struck a teaspoon against a mug to send the actors on. The bell is fixed now, but opening night still starts with tea.

mbm-2452.clue: Our first bass player was a broom handle.
mbm-2452.quote: I built a washtub bass for our first band rehearsal. The note changes when I lean on the stick. My little brother says I dance like a man trying to start an old car.

mbm-2453.clue: The little red light beat the streetlights.
mbm-2453.quote: I fixed an old ham set by the window. The first voice came through at dusk just as the power went out next door. Our battery lamp and that red radio light kept us company till morning.

mbm-2454.clue: The boss fight lasts two bus stops.
mbm-2454.quote: My handheld game froze halfway through a jump on the bus. I held it exactly level till my stop. A kid two seats back got off early just to see whether I landed.

mbm-2455.clue: We drew the whole dungeon on a tablecloth.
mbm-2455.quote: I got lost playing a maze game, so my cousin traced the corners onto an old cloth in washable marker. On laundry day the whole castle vanished and we got to discover it again.

mbm-2456.clue: My tee fits in my shirt buttonhole.
mbm-2456.quote: I carved a tee from a twig on the first course Dad let me play. It's too short to hit from now. I tuck it in my collar when he comes to watch.

mbm-2457.clue: Our airfield keeps its arrivals on the fence.
mbm-2457.quote: At the flying club's open day we tied a ribbon to the fence for every plane we saw land. Gran brought one tiny blue ribbon for the plane she'd learned in fifty years ago. I tied mine beside it when the old biplane came home.

mbm-2458.clue: A potato started my first campfire story.
mbm-2458.quote: Rain kept us in the tent with an unbaked potato. I drew a face on it and gave it a deep voice. My cousins still insist he gets the first line every trip.

mbm-2459.clue: My hook has one good squeak.
mbm-2459.quote: Gran's crochet hook rubs against my ring on every third stitch. When I made her a blanket she knew which part I'd finished just by listening from the next room.

mbm-2460.quote: I hike every gorge path slowly because I stop to draw the water. My left shoe always gets soaked leaning over the safe rail. The right one comes home looking like a spectator.

mbm-2461.clue: My station has an orange peel on the shelf.
mbm-2461.quote: A radio friend described his favorite marmalade recipe in Morse so slowly I could write it down. I stuck the peel from my first batch beside the logbook. Transmitting smells is my next project.

mbm-2462.clue: I tie the loose end in a figure eight.
mbm-2462.quote: I run with a friend who hates starting. At our gate he ties a tiny eight in my lace and says we'll untie it when we finish a loop. Somehow we always make it back.

mbm-2463.clue: Our first wrestling match lasted until the kettle boiled.
mbm-2463.quote: I tried to fold a king-size quilt by myself and disappeared under it. Our quilting circle found me by my slippers. Now we snap the finished quilts open together in the yard. The dog still noses every pair of slippers first.

mbm-2464.quote: Gran lent me one pearl bead to sew onto my bowling bag. On league night I tap it for luck. She never asks my score first; she asks if her pearl had fun.

mbm-2465.clue: The heavy set smells like lavender.
mbm-2465.quote: My sister sewed little lavender sachets for our gym lockers. My lifting partner opens ours before the last set. We breathe in, spot each other and somehow the room feels like her garden.

mbm-2466.clue: My drafts live in a cookie tin.
mbm-2466.quote: I write a short story on scraps and pile them in a red tin. Opening it at midnight used to disappoint my brother. Now he pulls one out and reads before he checks for biscuits.

mbm-2467.clue: I saved the smallest slice for the winner.
mbm-2467.quote: At our melon contest my niece pointed out the winning melon had a crooked stripe. I cut her a sliver with that stripe still on it. She kept the rind like a little green trophy.

mbm-2468.clue: I measure from the dented side.
mbm-2468.quote: My uncle's old bocce ball has a shallow dent. Once a marigold petal stuck in it so neatly we left it there for the whole round. His orange ball kept flowering as it rolled.

mbm-2469.clue: My deck has one empty sleeve in front.
mbm-2469.quote: I keep a transparent sleeve for whatever card my kid brother draws me. Today it's an enormous purple snail. He says its special move is arriving late on purpose.

mbm-2470.clue: I follow the shadows of the statues.
mbm-2470.quote: In a new city I sketch statues by drawing only their shadows. My longest one was a little bronze pigeon at sunset. It stretched clear across a cafe doorstep.

mbm-2471.clue: I bought the wrong blue on purpose.
mbm-2471.quote: The paint shop sold me a tube of blue called rain. I painted our porch on the sunniest day of the year using only that blue and the white of the paper. My aunt asked for an umbrella.

mbm-2472.clue: My best climb started sitting down.
mbm-2472.quote: I practiced a low traverse with a friend who was new to climbing. We kept our shoes inches above the pads and talked our way sideways. We traveled farther than either of us would have dared up.

mbm-2473.clue: My sister's hat whistles in the wind.
mbm-2473.quote: I crocheted a hat with a spiral too open near one ear. On the ferry it made a faint whistle. She asked me to make her a matching one for the other ear.

mbm-2474.clue: The leaves go in before the flowers.
mbm-2474.quote: I crocheted a garland for the kitchen door. I ran out of red yarn after one blossom, so I hung the leaves anyway. Every birthday I add a flower in that person's favorite color.

mbm-2475.clue: My quilt starts with the underside of a collar.
mbm-2475.quote: I saved the unfaded cloth from under Dad's old collar. It's the smallest square in a much paler blue quilt. When I turn the corner over, I can see how bright that shirt looked on his first day.
